title: Modal verbs 6: might / may / could / must (guessing)
note: Might / may / could / must speculation. could = might / may here (not past ability). · Bank 48 · RUE2 TRANSPLANT 2026-08-25; intro+chips smoked 2026-08-30. · 2026-09-04 B1 loop: D1 — five explanations covered all 48 items (one of them 11), each now names its own modal phrase and whether the guess is about now or the past; A8 twin closed; A4 four Czech prompts gained the demonstrative that licenses their `the`; F3 `bug` was not on the path and is now `problem`.

cards.title: Modal verbs 6: might / may / could / must (guessing)
cards.title_cz: Modální slovesa 6: might / may / could / must (odhad)
points: A fact names reality: She works late.
A modal names a **mode**: She **might** work late.
**may** and **could** do the same job as **might**.
Nine modal verbs: can, could, may, might, must, shall, should, will, would.

cards.title: Degrees of certainty
points: **might** / **may** / **could** sit in the middle.
All three mean possible. **could** is not past ability.

cards.title: The nine modals — map

rows: The lights are on. She **must** be home.
He **can't** be at work. It's Sunday.

points: **might**, **may**, **could** are one job here: a guess.
The others have different jobs.

cards.title: What is modality?
points: is it possible?
is it necessary?
English often shows this with a modal, not only with words like maybe / probably.

rows: Czech often uses možná / určitě / nemůže být
A modal shows how sure the speaker is

cards.title: What modals do to a sentence
points: 1) Meaning: possibility / certainty / impossibility — a guess from evidence
2) Form: next verb stays base — *might go*, not *might goes*
3) Questions and negatives use the modal: *Could she…?*
A modal does three practical jobs at once:

table.caption: Same situation, different stance
rows: impossible (we just saw him at work)

cards.title: Form
points: No -s on the main verb: She **might live** here (not lives)
No to: **must be** (not must to be)
Past: **might have** gone · **must have** seen — not might went
Present guess: modal + base. Past guess: modal + have + past participle.

cards.title: Not obligation
points: Obligation / advice was A2 must / should.

rows: You must wear a seatbelt. (= rule / strong need)
B1 speculation: The lights are on
she must be home. (= I conclude)
I conclude… not I have to

cards.title: Czech trap · možná
points: Czech often puts možná once; English chooses a modal on the verb.
**might** / **may** / **could** all fit Czech možná.
